newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank profit growth seen slowing after big first half.
newsitem.headline: Maybank profit growth seen slowing after big first half.

text.p: Earnings growth for Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) is likely to slow in the second half of its financial year after an impressive 39 percent jump in group net profit in the first two quarters, analysts said.

The country's biggest banking group on Saturday reported a net profit of 654.57 million ringgit ($262.8 million) in the first half of its year ending June 30, 1997, up from 469.69 million ringgit in the previous period.
The results exceeded forecasts by most analysts who were expecting a net profit of about 580-600 million ringgit.
"It was a very good set of results. It caught most of us by surprise," said Gan Kim Khoon, research manager of SocGen Crosby Research in Kuala Lumpur.
Soon Teck Onn, banking analyst at ING-Barings, said the first half results were exceptional but the performance was unlikely to be repeated in the second half.
"A lot of the profits came from margin expansion. I don't think there will be any further expansion and growth should be slower in the second half," he said.
But despite the expected slower earnings growth, analysts said earlier forecasts of Maybank's full-year profits would have to be revised upward.
"I expect a five to 10 percent upward revision," Soon said.

Analysts polled by the Estimate Directory have forecast net profit at an average 1.26 billion ringgit for the current year ending June 30, 1997. Maybank posted a 1.07 billion ringgit net profit last year.
Maybank managing director Amirsham Aziz attributed the strong performance in the first half to operational efficiency, better interest margins and more loans.
He said interest margins improved by 51 basis points while loan growth was maintained at 17 percent. Analysts had expected a slower loan growth of 10-15 percent.
Amirsham said he expected steady loan growth in the second half.

Apart from Maybank, which again contributed the bulk of the group's earnings, good results were also seen in other subsidiaries, including 75 percent-owned Kwong Yik Bank Bhd which the bank is selling for 2.16 billion ringgit.
Analysts said Kwong Yik Bank might account for only three months of the group's profits in the second half as the sale to stockbroking group Rashid Hussain Bhd is expected to be completed by March.
"But they will be cash-rich very soon and it will be interesting to see how they make use of the money to compensate for the loss of Kwong Yik Bank," said Desmond Ch'ng of South Johor Securities.
He said he expected some re-rating of Maybank stock but "it will be minor".
"I believe the results have been factored into the stock which had risen quite sharply over the past week. It looks a bit expensive at the current level," Ch'ng said.
Maybank stock closed on Friday at 27.75 ringgit, up from 26.00 the previous week.
